question: Which sport contributed the most gold medals to India in the Olympics?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Hockey**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Hockey** is the sport that has contributed the highest number of gold medals to **India** in the history of the **Olympic Games**. Out of the **10 gold medals** India has won in total, **8 gold medals** have been secured by the **Indian Men’s Field Hockey Team**. *Hence, the correct answer is Hockey.*
 
• The **Indian Men’s Hockey Team** maintained an extraordinary winning streak, capturing **six consecutive gold medals** from **1928 to 1956**. They added two more gold medals to their tally in the **1964 Tokyo Olympics** and the **1980 Moscow Olympics**.
 
• **Shooting** has contributed **1 gold medal** to India’s tally. This was achieved by **Abhinav Bindra** in the **10m Air Rifle** event during the **2008 Beijing Olympics**. While a significant achievement, it is far fewer than the medals won in hockey. *Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.*
 
• **Badminton** has brought **India** three Olympic medals (one silver and two bronze) through athletes like **Saina Nehwal** and **PV Sindhu**, but the country has yet to win a **gold medal** in this discipline. *Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.*
 
• **Boxing** has contributed **3 bronze medals** to India’s Olympic history, won by **Vijender Singh** (2008), **Mary Kom** (2012), and **Lovlina Borgohain** (2020). However, no **gold medal** has been won in boxing. *Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **The Golden Era of Indian Hockey**: India’s dominance in field hockey is legendary. The team won its first-ever gold at the **1928 Amsterdam Olympics**. The legendary player **Major Dhyan Chand**, often called the **Wizard of Hockey**, played a crucial role in the **1928, 1932, and 1936** victories.
 
• **Post-Independence Success**: The **1948 London Olympics** marked the first time **Independent India** won an Olympic gold medal, defeating **Great Britain** in the final. This was followed by gold medals in **1952 (Helsinki)** and **1956 (Melbourne)**.
 
• **Individual Gold Medalists**: For many decades, India only had team gold medals in hockey. **Abhinav Bindra** became the first Indian to win an **individual gold medal** in **2008**. The second individual gold was won by **Neeraj Chopra** in **Athletics (Javelin Throw)** at the **2020 Tokyo Olympics**.
 
• **Recent Hockey Revival**: After a gap of **41 years** without an Olympic medal in hockey, the **Indian Men’s Team** won a **Bronze medal** at the **2020 Tokyo Olympics** and repeated the feat with another **Bronze** at the **2024 Paris Olympics**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Total Medal Count**: As of the conclusion of the **2024 Paris Olympics**, India has won a total of **41 Olympic medals**. This includes **10 Gold**, **10 Silver**, and **21 Bronze** medals.
 
• **Linguistic and Cultural Impact**: Because of the massive success in the early 20th century, **Field Hockey** is often colloquially referred to as the **National Game of India**, although the government has not officially declared any sport as such.
 
• **Transition to AstroTurf**: India’s decline in hockey dominance after the **1970s** is often attributed to the introduction of **artificial grass (AstroTurf)**, which changed the speed and style of the game, favoring European power-based play over Indian skill-based dribbling.
 
• **First Female Medalist**: While hockey leads in gold, it is important to note that **Karnam Malleswari** was the first Indian woman to win an Olympic medal (**Bronze** in **Weightlifting**) at the **2000 Sydney Olympics**.
